I’ve been playing Left 4 Dead 2 since it first came out on the Xbox 360, and I’ve put an absolutely stupid amount of time into this game. Now I own it on Steam, and naturally I had to come back and slaughter some Zeds with a bunch of my friends.

Back on the Xbox 360, I used to think I was the GOAT. I thought I had the sauce. I thought I had the flow. I thought I was untouchable.

Then I played with Doug.

BRO’S GOT THE SAUCE.
BRO’S GOT THE FLOW.
BRO’S GOT THE DOUGH.

When it comes to killing Zeds and stopping them dead in their tracks, Doug absolutely has it figured out. Watching this man work makes me question every hour I’ve ever put into this game.

BUT…

Bro still doesn’t know how to B-hop. 💀

And then there’s the Steam Workshop.

♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.

The Steam Workshop for this game is unbeatable. The amount of ridiculous, hilarious, completely unhinged mods you can put into this game is incredible. I ended up turning my entire game into HALO, because apparently Left 4 Dead 2 needed Master Chief fighting zombies. 😂

And somehow… it works.

That’s what makes this game so damn fun. You can play it seriously, play it with your friends, completely ruin the game with stupid mods, or turn the entire thing into another franchise.

Overall Rating! 
Broke my God dang scale!
You Cannot go wrong playing this game, unless you are competing against Doug

reviews.author: Eyesore
reviews.review:
[h1]Vampire Survivors[/h1]

This is the game that defined the genre. Technically it's a good game, but it will eat up all the time you have, as each run takes around 30 minutes, depending on how long you survive, of course.

If you want to find everything in the game or get the different evolutions, then you need to check your Grimoire often, perhaps also check a guide for the best builds so you know what weapon combinations you need, and then hope you'll get lucky. In terms of gameplay, there isn't much there besides walking around, choosing weapons/skills and exploring areas with question marks. There are some hidden areas, some of which can be hard to find if you're not checking everything.

I can't play more than one or two runs at a time because I don't feel like I'm making much progress. The game will give you new characters and areas to play with, so that's nice, but again, you need to think about what kind of build you want to use with each character.

Is it a fun game? At times, when you've got your build together and are plowing through enemies, sure. But I guess there must be something wrong with my dopamine receptors, because I just can't keep myself positively engaged with this game for a long time. Each run has more intensive and less intensive phases, and usually when the enemy types change, there's a large drop in enemy numbers and in how quickly you level up. What you want from each run happens probably in just a few crucial minutes, for example when you decide what weapons and skills you'll use. But the rest of the time is mostly just walking around.

So perhaps check it out for a few hours to see if you like it, but honestly you will probably either like it or hate it depending on whether the grind clicks with you.

Final score: 6/10

reviews.author: squirrelly_joe
reviews.review:
Valheim is one of the best games I've ever played, and it stands at the top of the "survival" genre. For those wondering if it lives up to the hype or if you should invest the time, let me give you a simple breakdown of the game's strengths and weaknesses:

Strengths:

This game has AMBIENCE like few you've ever played! The intentionally lo-fi visuals are somehow absolutely gorgeous! It also has a wonderful soundtrack, which perfectly fits the vibe of the game. Sometimes I'll just sit there on the porch of my self-built cabin in the meadows and watch a thunderstorm, enjoying the cozy vibes. I know it's strange to call a game about Viking purgatory "cozy" but there are times when the game genuinely feels that way.

There's also a MASSIVE amount of content. This game is intentionally designed to be played for hundreds  of hours if you want. You can, of course, sprint through each biome, straight to the boss if you're skilled enough. But to me, that feels like it would defeat the purpose of the game. This journey is meant to be enjoyed, not rushed.

If you enjoy a challenge, you'll find no shortage of it in Valheim. When played on default settings, the game can be BRUTALY punishing at times. There's nothing like painstakingly building a boat, sailing to an unfamiliar biome, and being 1-shotted by a new enemy, thus losing your boat and all your gear until you can reclaim it. I'll talk more about this in the negatives, but the positive side is: the difficulty is highly customizable. There are plenty of options so you can enjoy the game however you like.

There are a ton of weapons and builds to experiment with, and there's something for most any playstyle. Bear in mind, that some weapons are locked behind progression, so don't feel bad if you need to consult the wiki to figure out what you're working toward. 

Valheim really does give a sense of pure exploration like few games I've played before, and I find the world incredibly immersive! You can fight, you can farm, you can sail; there's honestly so much to do that it's hard to cover in a short review like this.

Whether you like building a massive base to call home, or want to venture forth and slay the enemies of Odin, this game has something for most any gamer!

Now for the negatives:

I mentioned earlier how punishing this game can be. When played on default settings, you can't take many items through portals (and the map is HUGE), you lose most of your gear on each death, and your skills are lowered slightly as well. All in all, it makes a default-settings playthough pretty brutal. For these reasons, I personally recommend pulling back the difficulty a little for your first attempt. 

The game's many mechanics are... KIND OF explained, but there's a ton of nuance that most new players will miss entirely. In fact, the game can be a tad obtuse if you don't know what you're doing. Valheim has a wonderfully welcoming community, so you'll find no shortage of help if you need it, but it can be a big learning curve for a new player.

And finally, the game is a touch lacking in QOL features. No "stack to nearby chests" no "craft from nearby chests", ladders are somehow the most awkward thing you've ever used, and certain activities still just feel a little clunky.

However, in spite of the negatives, this game is still incredible! My advice would be this: find an experienced player to give you a few tips, then go in with some goals in mind. Are you a casual player who's content to only make gradual progress while you build a mansion for yourself? Or are you a sweaty tryhard who wants to beat all the bosses ASAP?

Have some idea of what you want to get out of the game going in, adjust the world settings accordingly, and have fun!

May Odin look favorably on your quest!

reviews.author: Rampage
reviews.review:
Recommended
Overall Rating: 8/10

Devil May Cry 5 is an absolute masterclass in character action games. The RE Engine delivers breathtaking visuals, and the combat loop is arguably the best the genre has ever seen. Swapping between Nero, V, and Dante keeps the gameplay feeling fresh, and the soundtrack dynamically pumps up alongside your style rank to deliver an incredible adrenaline rush. It is a triumphant return for the franchise that veterans and newcomers alike will love.

However, the PC port isn't entirely perfect. I occasionally experienced a frustrating audio desync problem during both the cinematic cutscenes and actual gameplay. During heavy action or camera angle changes, the audio would occasionally stutter or lag behind the visual animations.

Quick fix for anyone experiencing this: Go to your Steam game folder, open dmc5config.ini, and change Capability=DirectX12 and TargetPlatform=DirectX12 to DirectX11. This partially resolved the sync and micro-stutter issues for me!)

Even with the occasional technical hiccup, the phenomenal gameplay and high replay value make this an easy recommendation. A solid 8/10 and a must-play for hack-and-slash fans.

reviews.review:
Even years after its release, Cities: Skylines remains the absolute gold standard for city-building and traffic management simulation, easily outclassing newer alternatives in stability and content.

Traffic Simulation & Infrastructure: At its core, this is a masterclass in urban planning and logistics. Balancing highway intersections, roundabouts, cargo trains, and public transit systems is both a brutal challenge and immensely satisfying when traffic flow hits 80%+.

God-Tier Modding Community: The Steam Workshop breathes infinite life into this title. From essential quality-of-life tools like Traffic Manager (TM:PE) and Move It to photorealistic assets, mods transform this game from a casual sandbox into an architectural canvas.

Deep City Mechanics: Managing zoned demand (RCI), budget allocation, public services, natural disasters, and district policies gives you genuine control over how your metropolis evolves.

Traffic AI can be quirky without mods, but with the Workshop at your disposal, no other city builder comes close to this level of creative and managerial freedom.

Verdict: 9.5/10 – A must-play masterpiece for any strategy and simulation fan.

reviews.review:
Игра 'Siege Hammer' – это приятное сочетание стратегии, менеджмента и элементов Tower Defense. Мне понравился фокус на строительстве и развитии крепости, а также необходимость тщательно планировать оборону, учитывая различные типы врагов и их слабости. Система развития юнитов и технологий добавляет глубины игровому процессу.

Графика выполнена в симпатичном, мультяшном стиле, что создает расслабляющую атмосферу, несмотря на напряженные битвы. Интерфейс интуитивно понятен, что позволяет быстро освоиться и начать строить свою неприступную крепость.

Однако, игра могла бы предложить больше контента. Некоторые уровни кажутся повторяющимися, а разнообразие врагов со временем становится недостаточным. Было бы здорово увидеть больше уникальных юнитов и оборонных сооружений, а также расширенную кампанию с интересным сюжетом.

В целом, 'Siege Hammer' – это увлекательная игра, которая может затянуть на несколько часов. Рекомендую ее любителям жанра, и надеюсь на дальнейшие обновления и улучшения.

reviews.author: Obey the Fist!
reviews.review:
"Siege Hammer" is a simple lightweight VR minigame, basically a tower defense but the developer felt TD games would be better if they had really awkward VR controls.

The graphics in this game are passable, but could be better.  And while it's vital for any game to have impressive visuals (gaming is a visual medium, after all), there's more to a game than just the graphics.  To be worth a gamers time, the game must match top tier visuals with top tier gameplay, and that's not happening here.

It's VR exclusive, and that shows the developer failed to understand the most basic axiom of VR game design... if the only cool thing about your product is VR support, your product is not cool.  This compares very poorly to other TD games on Steam, and seems to have been made VR exclusive just to try protect the game from failing that comparison by keeping it out of the hands of the majority of gamers.

It's free... now, but it wasn't before.  The developer was charging $15 USD for this (!!!!).  Price barriers, especially on low quality products, can be a direct cause of failure.  It's a nice gesture for the game to be given away for free, but it also tells us that the game wasn't good enough to succeed as a paid product.

Even though this is "free", it failed to appeal to the 120 million+ gamers on Steam.  SteamDB showed the game peaked at only 3 concurrent players... this is a dismal public reception.  This was so bad they couldn't even give it away.

Bearing in mind that free games don't add +1 to your game collector count, should you bother adding this to your library and downloading it?

Not this time.  This isn't worth downloading.  While this won't cost you any money, you get what you pay for, and sometimes, even when the game is free, it's still not enough.

[h1] Experienced on the Oculus Rift with Touch Controllers [/h1]

So this game went free to play last April 2018 ... I can see why. It's just a very mediocre Tower Defense without much inspiration as far as the gameplay. A lot of the controls are just point and click, even this Siege hammer that you have on your hand. You think you can hammer it down with your motion controlllers? Nope ... That's pretty much all you do during the game. Point and click TD game. Which is sad because there was a very nice start to the game with nicely done cinematic scenes. But the gameplay is just very drab. There was no challenge at all and it was all pretty mindless. And just getting out of the first level felt very grindey. The animations weren't the best either as you couldn't really see how your defenses were doing & sometimes they looked like they were just sitting there. And there was never any sense that you might be in danger.

The hardest part was just staying awake through the whole thing. 

Rate 5/10. It mean it is free. Could be nice for a mindless time waster.

Once I could easily beat them there didn't seem like any reason to grind out the more advanced stuff. I didn't see anything that I needed to power up to take on. I could have gotten into the grind to customize a freighter or base or do fleet missions, or any number of things. But none of it was really calling to me. I'm sure that I will come back at some point and try again. But for now I'm content to put it down. But that's still 60 hours of enjoyment and I think most anyone will find at least that much enjoyment in the game as well.

Let me start by saying that I do truly *love* this game. I love the way you are forced to learn ghost behaviors and work with a team to accomplish tasks. I love how liberating it feels to finally be able to play no evidence rounds with relative ease sometimes. I've spent hundreds of hours on Phasmo and made countless and cherished memories. However, I both do and don't recommend this game right now, and here's why:

With that said, holy hell... the game continues to be spontaneously unplayable. Ghost behaviors randomly malfunction (Shade being super active AND hunting while you're in the room, for example - one of many) and it makes it nearly impossible to accurately guess the ghost. And then you have the evidence... I should not be waiting 30+ minutes for a single piece of evidence, and I definitely shouldn't be waiting indefinitely for the last piece of evidence while playing on Professional or below. I am constantly having to guess the ghost because the evidence won't show up after 40m - 1hr+ of gameplay.

Every update seems to create more problems than it fixes. Lagging, game crashes, bugs, items not working (such as the incense refusing to light or even if it does, not working on the ghost).

I implore the devs to *PLEASE* spend more time on getting these issues worked out. I struggle to find friends to play this with right now because of how broken every other match feels.

I also would love to see an 'OG' section for old maps, as I desperately miss the old Tanglewood and farmhouses...

reviews.author: JayDaScoobs
reviews.review:
I have mixed feelings about the recent Phasmophobia updates. Unfortunately, I keep getting matched with extremely toxic players. I can't tell if it's the community or just bad luck, but in my experience it's safest not to talk in lobbies unless someone speaks to you first, because it often ends with a racial slur being thrown at me or one of my friends and it's repulsive. This happens in nearly every other match, and I shouldn't have to put up with it. One bad game wouldn't bother me, but the frequency wore me down. Phasmophobia is a game about hunting ghosts, and I wish the conversation would stay there.

What bothers me most is how many people in this community seem to think racism is funny. Racism is never funny, in any context, and if you think it is, you are part of the problem. It points to a bigger underlying issue, and I don't understand how it has gone unaddressed for so long. Popular creators rarely speak up about it, and the behavior is seldom called out by players or the people running the game, so it just keeps going.

Optimization also seems to be getting worse with each update. To be clear, the game runs great on my newer rig, at over 420 FPS, so if you have a newer card you're fine, it feels about as light as running a browser on the side it's that smooth. On my older system, though, it struggled badly, even though I've seen players with weaker rigs holding a steady 30 FPS. I couldn't manage that, so between the performance and the matchmaking, I uninstalled. SO I wouldn't suggest buying or playing this game with something like a GTX 1650 which is the bare minimum atleast these days if not a 2080 Super so optimization still is horrible. Not everybody can upgrade every generation.

What I wish for most is a game that feels cooperative. A co-op game should make people want to work together, and that starts with being welcoming to newer players. Phasmophobia has a steep learning curve, and plenty of people don't have time to study ghost types and evidence on top of school, work, or a college degree they're trying to finish. New players shouldn't be pushed out or made to feel stupid for not knowing everything yet. If the community focused on teaching and encouraging each other instead of tearing each other down, this could be a great game. As it stands, I can't recommend a co-op game that so rarely feels cooperative.

That said, I have had, and still occasionally have, good times in this game. I've met great people who also try to avoid those kinds of lobbies, and some of them have resorted to hosting their own private or public lobbies just so they can control who stays and kick the toxic players, because they don't want to deal with that. I still believe the game has real potential as something to play with your own friends. If you're going to pick a co-op game, this is a much better choice for your friend group than most of the throwaway party or "slop" games out there, and that's always a great idea. Otherwise, I really struggle to love the current state of the community and the recent updates, especially the changes to the maps.

reviews.author: UmbraVulpe
reviews.review:
Hogwarts Legacy: um castelo lindo com um jogo vazio dentro

Hogwarts Legacy vende um sonho e entrega um passeio. A ambientação é excelente, e esta é, sem dúvida, a melhor versão de Hogwarts já feita, superior à dos filmes. O problema é que quase tudo fora da escola é vazio.

A história é rasa, genérica e sem peso. Os personagens são fracos e sem presença, e ninguém deixa marca. O combate é raso e repetitivo, e os puzzles são fáceis e infantis ao extremo. O mapa é enorme para tão pouco a se fazer nele, e as side quests ficam maçantes com o passar das horas.

O sistema de criação de animais parece preso em fase alpha: tem uma ideia inicial, mas foi abandonado antes de virar algo. O crafting é ruim, pois raramente serve para algo além de melhorar equipamentos que o jogo, por ser fácil demais, nunca exige.

Veredito: não vale a pena como jogo de campanha. Vale apenas como "simulador de passear em Hogwarts".

Para os ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥:

Hogwarts Legacy: a gorgeous castle with an empty game inside

Hogwarts Legacy sells a dream and delivers a sightseeing tour. The setting is excellent, and this is undoubtedly the best version of Hogwarts ever made, better than the films. The problem is that almost everything outside the school is empty.

The story is shallow, generic and weightless. The characters are weak and forgettable, and none of them leave a mark. Combat is shallow and repetitive, and the puzzles are painfully easy and childish. The map is huge for how little there is to do in it, and the side quests turn tedious as the hours pass.

The creature-keeping system feels stuck in its alpha stage: it has an initial idea, but was abandoned before becoming anything. Crafting is poor, since it is rarely useful beyond upgrading gear the game, being too easy, never requires.

Verdict: not worth it as a campaign game. Worth it only as a "Hogwarts walking simulator".

reviews.author: Risk
reviews.review:
It pains me to do this, but this has been one of the times where a game I have brutally disliked the optics of has surprised me and become one of the more addictive games in my roster for the year. My friend bought this game for me because it came out as cross platform, and as it is there are only like 45 games to play together on pc with people on PS5 so I decided I would try it even though I have had no prior interest in it, so I only play this game with my friends on PS5 but it has been a great time with tons of funny moments and stress over mechanics of the game shared between us. The parody aspect is something I don't really care for, the whole "it's like Pokémon with guns" argument never really made me care any more than I didn't already, because I never really wanted to shoot a Pokémon to begin with I liked having them as companions that's like the whole point. BUT if ANYONE had told me prior that this game ran almost like a carbon copy for the gameplay of ARK; Survival Evolved, I would have instantly become more drawn in as I spent my childhood glued to Ark. The gameplay is fun because it is basically a mixture of Ark, Zelda BOTW, and Pokémon, with most of the more fun aspects of each taken and put into the game. The gameplay loop itself gets annoying and stressful until you get enough pals to start automating things and there are a lot of points I have reached especially late game where by the point I unlock one new building material to start crafting and get the materials for it ready to use, I have already leveled up enough to learn the next material, it almost feels gimmicky and hard to pace yourself efficiently. My favorite part is the base building and all of the cool things you can do, I built an all purpose slums style base in the mountains that only extends vertically and my framerate suffers when I visit that base but it's worth it for how cool it looks. There are surprisingly a lot of really cool pals in the game, every once in a while you will run into a walking copyright strike and that doesn't speak to me as much but a lot of the original designs in this game are really good and give the same feeling that a mixture of generations of Pokémon had once given as well. Speaking of performance the game runs really well even on my hardware, some of the biggest issues I tend to have with the game come down to things like crafting speeds, and some of the default settings like the weight, durability, and expiration timers that don't exactly feel like they are of any benefit to keep on for experience in the same way you would experience it on another survival game, the bars all seem to be shorter than you would expect. Overall this game has actually pleasantly surprised me as I expected to fully hate it, but I have come around to enjoy the game very much becoming the main game that me and my console friends have played this year together.
(Gifted Game)

Pros:
[list]

Cons:

Overall I got a lot of enjoyment for very little money out of it. Due to the season pass and resource grind every mission feels like progress, no matter which you pick. reviews.review:
[h1]A Man, Reborn in Absurdity[/h1]

[b] MAJOR SPOILER WARNING: [/b] This review contains potential spoilers for [i]Disco Elysium[/i], including character details, dialogue and aspects of the story. Read at your own discretion. I'd strongly recommend finishing the game before proceeding.

There is something fascinating about a man who has forgotten everything and still chooses to care.

Lieutenant Double-Yefreitor Harrier Du Bois is, or [b]was[/b], a disaster of a human being by almost every conceivable measure. A drunkard, a walking corpse drinking himself to death for no apparent reason and, overall, a rather sorry excuse for a human being.

But here's the catch: beneath all that self-destruction lies an exceptional detective. 216 cases solved in 18 years is a phenomenal achievement. And then there's the title of Lieutenant Double-Yefreitor, earned in part by rejecting promotion twice, leaving him with a rather unusual standing among his peers.

For me, I chose to paint him as a jolly cop, someone who's good with kids, a social democrat who still believes the world is workable and isn't entirely doomed. A friend above all else, whether to his colleagues or to complete strangers. Despite all his ♥♥♥♥-ups, he's still somehow chivalrous.

[b]Harry is one of the most beautiful canvases in gaming.[/b] You get to paint him however you want, in whatever manner you see fit. All the [i]Skills[/i] he possesses are simply the colours you're given to paint him with. And what makes it so fascinating is that none of those colours necessarily define the final picture.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]A man is more than the sum of his mistakes.[/h2]

[i]"Something beautiful is going to happen."[/i]

[h2]A little something personal[/h2]

I don't think I've ever had a game resonate with me quite like this one. In a way, it pulled me out of my own head when I was spiralling a little too far into myself. It reminded me that, regardless of how badly things have gone or how much of ourselves we've lost along the way, we can still choose to begin again.

We can close an old book, leave it behind and start writing a new one. Not everything needs to be carried into the next chapter, and perhaps some pages are better left unread, never to be opened again.

I suppose that's what I'll take away from this game: the idea that it's never too late to become someone new.

reviews.review:
WARDOGS has a good idea at its core, but right now there isn't enough content to back it up, and the progression ruins it.

At the start you unlock a lot pretty quickly, and it feels great. Then it hits a wall. The gear that actually matters, like the M4, AP ammo and level 3 armour, is locked behind a huge amount of grinding, and you have to play a ridiculous number of matches to get there.

The problem is you're not grinding in a vacuum. The people who put in more hours get that gear before you, and it makes a massive difference. Next thing you know you're mag dumping into someone's level 3 armour with no effect, and they turn around and drop you with a silenced M4 and AP ammo. You didn't lose because they outplayed you. You lost because they've grinded more than you.

A shooter can get away with a grind if it has the content to keep you going, but WARDOGS doesn't have that yet. There's a good game in here somewhere, and I'd happily come back if the progression gets fixed and more content gets added. For now, I can't recommend it.

Comprehensive Analysis of Deep Flaws in CK3 Core Mechanics: Centralization vs. Eurocentric "Thug-State" Bias and Broken Pacing

Dear Crusader Kings 3 Development Team,

I am writing to express my profound frustration with a series of interlocking, deeply flawed design mechanics in Crusader Kings 3. When combined, these mechanics utterly ruin the experience of playing a highly centralized, legitimate bureaucratic empire (such as an Eastern/Confucian state) and turn a grand strategy experience into an exercise in arbitrary time-gating, systemic unfairness, and blatant double standards. 

I am an experienced player who recently stabilized a massive empire, only to find that the game engine actively cheats the player, rewards treason, and artificially cripples a civilization's timeline. There are three core areas where the game mechanics are profoundly broken:

1. The Culture Leader Time-Gating Nightmare (Stelling a Century of Progress)
The interaction between minor (child) rulers, AI hijacking of culture slots, and the mandatory 50-year cooldown timer is mechanically malicious. Here is the exact timeline of events from my campaign that demonstrates how the game engine steals 100 years of gameplay:
- Around 1150, my empire completed a culture tradition reform. Due to the 50-year cooldown, I was perfectly on track to reform my next core tradition around 1204.
- Right near 1204, my capable adult Emperor was assassinated, and Genghis Khan launched an invasion. My designated legal heir—a 5-year-old child—ascended the throne.
- Because the game hard-locks child rulers from being the Culture Leader, the title was instantly stripped from me and handed to an insignificant AI vassal who happened to hold a couple of counties of my culture.
- I spent the next 20 years in a brutal, multi-front war, managing a professional army of 34,000 elite troops against 100,000 rebels and repelling 50,000 Mongols.
- At around age 25, having successfully subjugated Genghis Khan and locked the rebels in my dungeon, I finally reclaimed the Culture Leader title.

However, upon opening the menu, I found the AI had queued up a completely useless, garbage tradition. The progress bar says it won't finish until 1240. Because I am forbidden from canceling an active AI project, and because a mandatory 50-year cooldown applies AFTER it finishes, I am locked out of researching my desired tradition until 1290. 

I was ready to research in 1204. Because of your child-lock and incompetent AI proxy, I must wait until 1290. That is nearly ONE HUNDRED YEARS completely stolen from the player through arbitrary time-gating.

2. The Broken Logic of National Rebellions and "Faction Immunity"
The game completely lacks historical accuracy regarding the political gravity of "Legitimacy" and "Rightful Succession" in centralized states. In a Confucian or high-centralization realm, a lawful crown prince succeeding the throne is a supreme moral anchor. Treason is an absolute, unforgivable crime ("乱臣贼子，人人得而诛之"). 

Yet in CK3, the moment a child inherits, the AI treats it as a green light for an unmitigated pirate-style plunder. Dozens of vassals representing vast swaths of the empire simultaneously rise in rebellion, acting like mindless profit-calculators rather than members of a bound legal and moral order. 

Worse yet, the game actively protects these criminals via arbitrary mechanical rules. In my campaign, after two years of grueling civil war, my war score reached 98%. Just one month away from an absolute 100% victory and mass-imprisonment of the traitors, the rebel faction leader suddenly died/committed suicide. 

The game immediately triggered a "War Invalidated" screen. The war abruptly ended. Because the specific ringleader was dead, the dozens of high-ranking co-conspirators who spent years burning my cities and slaughtering my soldiers were instantly granted full "faction immunity" and an automatic truce! They faced zero legal consequences, their lands could not be revoked, and they walked away scot-free to plot another coup. This is a severe mechanical failure that aggressively punishes the player's military victory.

3. Legitimizing Traitors While Criminalizing the Sovereign ("Protecting the Criminals")
The game mechanics enforce a bizarre double standard where rebels are coddled by the rules while the lawful sovereign is heavily penalized for enacting state justice. 
- If a claimant war breaks out and the player successfully assassinates or kills the puppet claimant, the war does not end. The game arbitrarily shifts the war's justification to an "Against Tyranny" war, allowing the rabid vassal AI to keep fighting seamlessly. The system insists the war *must continue* to favor the AI.
- Conversely, if the rebel general dies, the war *must stop* to shield the AI's co-conspirators.
- Furthermore, under doctrines like Confucianism, executing traitors who actively sought to destroy the Imperial line should inherently skyrocket the Emperor's Dread and Prestige, earning the praise of the common people for restoring law and order. Instead, the game's hard-coded criminal doctrines treat executing rebel relatives as "Kinslaying" and "Tyranny," imposing massive Piety and Prestige penalties on the victim (the Emperor). 

The game forces the player into a dystopian scenario where upholding the law makes *you* the criminal, while the system coddles actual traitors. Ironically, if a player adopts a primitive "Human Sacrifice" doctrine, the game happily rewards them with massive Piety for slaughtering captives, but penalizes a civilized Emperor for executing state traitors under civil law. This is a complete inversion of historical and legal logic.

Suggested Fixes:
1. Allow adult Culture Leaders to cancel an active AI-initiated tradition project, resetting the queue upon reclaiming their rightful title.
2. Fix the faction system so that when a faction leader dies during a civil war, the war transfers to a co-conspirator or results in an unconditional surrender of all participants, rather than invalidating the war and pardoning traitors.
3. Scale faction rebellion frequencies down significantly once an Empire unlocks advanced inheritance laws like Primogeniture and High Crown Authority, reflecting the actual historical stability of centralized systems.
4. Overhaul criminal and kinslaying doctrines so that executing vassals who are actively imprisoned for treason/rebellion does not trigger tyranny or kinslaying penalties.

A player should not have to rely on the debug console (`~`) to manually execute `set_culture_tradition` or `imprison_all_faction_members` just to inject basic fairness and historical sanity back into the game engine. Please address these glaring flaws in your upcoming development cycles.

Sincerely,
A Deeply Frustrated CK3 Sovereign

Overall I am really enjoying this game. As someone who sews IRL I can see this as a great game to let your kiddos play before letting them lay out patterns and cut up irl fabric. It doesn't teach you what "Grain" is or why it matters, but it does give you points for laying a pattern on the grain correctly and it will help highlight how important it is to be strategic with your placements to minimize waste. 

Things I love:
-Pattern placement - it tickles all my happy brain spots seeing as little fabric as possible get wasted
-Creative freedom within commissions
-How easy it is to restart sewing on a piece if you've gone off track
-No math involved! 
-If you remapped your controls you could easily play with just the mouse - which makes it a friendly game for our disabled friends! 


Things that mildly annoy me: 
-The music - I had to turn it off completely. Very repetitive.
-Setting the mannequin *every* time - very tedious
-Lack of accessory options (Perhaps I just have not unlocked them all yet?)
-You don't get bonus points (or money) for accessorizing an outfit. Often meaning that unless you just want to make is super pretty, its a waste of time to sit there and lay piping/lace/gems because you don't earn extra for making the dresses fancy looking.
-Prudence 
-anticlimactic ending with each dress you've made. They thank you then that's the end of it. This however, I can understand would require a lot more work for the devs so its just a mild "Aww if only you could see them wear it!" 
- you can ONLY make dresses. I'd love to make a cute pantsuit or shirt/pant situation.

QOL changes I'd love to see happen
- Some sort of  "Click" for the measurements when you're setting it on the mannequin or perhaps let us use the scroll wheel on the mouse to go up and down in measurements. I find clicking and dragging to be super tedious. 
- Please let us filter our cut pattern pieces by Front/Back/Skirt/Shirt/Sleeves. I am sick of scrolling through the list looking for all my front pieces then all my back pieces or being stuck to turn my mannequin around endlessly. 
-A visual L or R in the corner by our cut pattern pieces so we don't have to hover over if we're looking to complete a particular piece. (Could also add F and B for front and back if adding in a filter option is too difficult)
-More defined "how much fabric needed" perhaps something like  "Underskirt uses xyz, over skirt uses xyz" so when we're planning multiple fabrics we don't have to guess how much for each.
- a way to go back if we've hit "Draft" too soon or by accident and let us redraft it. 
- When we "Reset filters" PLEASE DONT LET THE FILTER BOX CLOSE!!!!!!!!!! This is so tedious, now I have to go back and click the filter button. 
-If we only have a few set characters -  WHY CAN I NOT SAVE THEIR MEASURMENTS? Why must I reset their mannequin each time? Please let me save their measurements for future use. 
- there HAS to be a better way for us to lay out lace or lay feathers, there just HAS to be.

reviews.author: Nightmarian
reviews.review:
The tl;dr so far is that the game is good but not great if you're a Control fan or a big fan of SCP-adjacent stuff and mediocre if you're anyone else.

Best part by far is, as always for Remedy, the visual presentation (not just graphics) and the insane environmental storytelling that comes from it.

Also kinda as always, the worst part is by far the combat system. Remedy really sucks at combat, and while they do come up with creative gimmicks, they generally do a poor job of integrating it with the gameplay loop and then evolving combat over the game so it stays fresh. That was one of the biggest complaints already from professional reviewers: combat gets repetitive fast, enemy variation is decent but barely expands per faction over ruunetime. Not only that, as they felt obligated to shoehorn in RPG systems instead of just making this an action game, you eventually power creep to godhood midway through the game and completely trivialize the combat system.

Mmmmkay… I guess there’s a reason this is ranging mid to upper ~80 overall, and remember kids that “professional” reviewers overrate. We’ll see how the game changes but right now I’m feeling it’s going to land somewhere near 75-80 for me.

Well, luckily for us this isn’t a soulslike utterly dependent on the core gameplay loop including combat to carry it, and as such, if you put story above all else, this is definitely worth playing. The classic Remedy world-building and environmental storytelling is back here in force, and simply “experiencing” the game is as always a delight, as it’s like literally walking through a wonderland gasping at everything. Squinting at clear references and trying to piece together other mysteries like an SCP agent yourself is also a lot of fun, as is simply engaging with all the supernatural elements.

Unfortunately, Remedy’s character and dialogue writing remains as garbage as always, so very few characters are memorable (including Dylan, sadly enough…) and simply serve as vehicles for your experience. However, it’s serviceable and realistic to a degree, so it does fit the setting. There are a few examples where the game tries to give you a ‘quirky’ character that you end up wishing had been killed by the Hiss, but it’s rare and most of the time the worst sin is that everything they do and say is boring which maybe is best since you already have a ton of insane bs happening all around you.

Gameplay-wise is definitely where the game gets slapped with its sub 90 score and is what in my opinion prevents this from being a real GOTY candidate. Best take on this I saw is Skill Up’s summary of “The game has a lot of flaws and does individual things imperfectly, but they still add up to an utterly worthwhile experience.” I feel a lot like that so far… yeah the dialogue sucks, yeah the characterization is bland, yeah combat is stiff, basic, and already getting boring and will probably only get more so as I power creep… but I’m still gasping when I run into some alternate realm, or get baited by some magical thing, or glance around at the fing craziness that New York becomes.

It’s definitely a game worth playing, especially if you loved the first Control (though so far it’s a poor sequel to it imo), and THANK GOD Remedy was sane enough to not only put it on Steam but also only charge $60. I very much think it’s worth it full price.

So why the downvote? Well, I wish there was a mixed option… I very much feel this game has little broad appeal, and think most people will eventually get bored and stop playing it midday through, and I can already see why as I'm watching youtube videos on my other screen myself half the playtime to stave off the boredom. Heck, I already know the ending is probably just going to be ambiguous inconclusive sequel bait we’ll have to wait another 10 years to get more ambiguous sequel bait for; it’s just how the setting is. 

However, if you just want to see zany going on, mull and gush over SCP-adjacent shiz in a AAA game for once, and don’t mind some weak elements like combat, this game is still very much worth it.

However, for everyone else, there are so many other games already out or coming soon that you should really think hard before committing.

Will update if I feel differently by the end. Let’s see.

reviews.author: That Brutal Guy
reviews.review:
This game is mind-blowing. Much like the first game, it's a great game premise with fantastic execution. The world is strange and doesn't try to bog you down with the details: things are paranormal, everything is weird, and you have to roll with the punches. That said, there's an internal logic to the world so that even the strangest stuff feels "believable." Combat is fun and rewarding, and you can tell the devs worked hard to balance out the weaponry and fighting styles. The graphics are great-- I play on a dinky 5+ year old game laptop, and this game still looks amazing. I'm sure on better PCs, this looks FANTASTIC, haha!

The best part about the game-- and something I haven't seen enough-- is that the [b]game's difficulty can be scaled to your needs.[/b] I play games for the story, the characters, and the world-- the combat is fun, but NOT my main draw to any type of game. To that end, if you get overwhelmed by battles/fights easily, you can adjust your damage output, damage you take, lag time on "perfect" dodges... the fights are wildly customizable between wanting wanting a [i]very[/i] tiny adjustment in how much damage you put out, all the way up to walking through the game like undying one-shot god, lmao. (Or, if you're a true masochist, you can totally nerf yourself and beef up enemies to the max. It's all about how much pain you like to feel when your play, haha!) Don't be intimidating into not getting this game just because people say the combat is difficult!

I just love that this game is so accessible to every type of gamer. There is SO, SO SO MUCH TO LOVE about this world, the gameplay, the visuals, the characters, the music, the whole freakin' experience-- and you don't need to love combat to enjoy what this Control has to offer. No matter your play style, if you like liminal spaces, kaleidoscopes, scary stories, SCPs, shadowy organizations, brown or gray stone spires, or being generally uncomfortable in the best way, this game is a devastating delight. I could NOT stop freakin' playing it. It makes me remember everything I loved about the first game. Just... what an absolutely fantastic and satisfying continuation of this amazing world. 10/10.

reviews.author: Fluffy Snowball
reviews.review:
WoW. Just WoW. Astounded. In my mind, what separates great games from exceptional ones is presentation, and this game doesn't lack in that department. The first one was amazing too, but this is just on a whole other level.
The passion and creativity behind this game are truly remarkable. Small disclaimer. This is in comparison to the first game mostly. Also, I miss the Ahti and more Board interactions in general. If this game does not win the GOTY award, I will be surprised.

Won't go in depth as I'm still enjoying my time, so the recency bias would be high, but some shallow/scrambled review is in order

Gameplay/World/Combat 9/10:
This is without a doubt the bread and butter of the game and truly the strongest aspect. The gameplay loop is satisfying enough, and whilst it has some dry points, besides one in particular (won't say because of the spoilers), none other overstay their welcome. The world and worldbuilding are amazing, and even at times it's a struggle to orient oneself, and some may be dizzy from it; it's still very unique and worth the motion sickness :) One other thing. To traverse certain levels, a player really must apply themselves in the moment and think fast, so don't play if your attention span is not in tip-top shape at that moment, as it might lead to frustration :) Also, love the addition of great music during certain moments. Regarding combat, it's a bit dry and simple at first, but it picks up after a while. And whilst there are weapon type combos that are better than others, it's overall satisfying enough. You get what you input. You can just mash one button and do pretty well, but you can do complex combos. Thing is, none of the enemies have enough HP to really survive a full combo and the juice to execute it is not worth it, so I resorted to the simplest button mashing in the end plus ignite and it yielded great results. 

Music/OST:  Disappointed/Great/10 :D
Zoe's Mixtape playlist is on repeat throughout the day mostly. I really have an issue with the deluxe edition not including the OST outside of the game; other than that, the moments where music is used in gameplay are amazing and elevate the scenes they are used in. Also, the song picked for the trailers are exceptional

Technical/Animations 8.5/10:
Just wanted to mention that whilst the environment seems less breakable than the original, the fact that the weapon parts stay temporarily after use is a very nice touch and really appreciated. Animations are executed rather well, besides the 360 spin in place, which looks rather awkward, but not something that hinders the experience, as it's not a sore eye and the game is fast-paced enough to not matter much. Other than that, animations are pretty solid and performance is acceptable

Story 8/10:
To me, the story has to be the weakest part. Don't get me wrong, the high points are extremely high, but the lowest are much lower than it would be expected. That said, it's still a very well-done story, but it has aspects/presentations from the first game missing, which would elevate it. Some of the side missions have better story moments than the main one at times. Also the response the player is presented with is a gamble; if you select a certain phrase/word, what the player character says is very different than what it's shown, which ruined certain moments for me

Fred is the absolute best!

reviews.author: comicGeek
reviews.review:
Played this game when it was first released on the PS3, and it was one of the most amazing experiences I had on that platform. The story was heartbreaking and hopeful at the same time. The sandboxed encounters were new and refreshing, keeping me glued to the screen. I later played the remastered version on PS4, and then again on PS5.

While every iteration delivered better graphics and enhanced the presentation, each replay only highlighted how dated the core game really is beneath the fresh coat of paint. Now on PC, not only are those design limits more noticeable and the linear story overly familiar, but technical issues constantly pull you out of the experience.

Most frustrating are the persistent crashes and freezes. They happen randomly, sometimes hours into a session, other times just minutes after booting up. Thankfully, mods exist to skip the exact scenes where these freezes occur; without them, I wouldn't have been able to finish the game at all.

Overall, the PC port is disappointing and ultimately soured the good memories I had from the PS3 era. It looks gorgeous, but replaying it under these conditions sucked all the joy out of it, and I only forced myself to finish it to cross it off my Steam backlog. If you have never experienced the game before, it is still worth playing, but pick up the PS5 version if you have that console. Otherwise, I wouldn't recommend it.

reviews.author: Nightheaven
reviews.review:
A fantastic sequel.

Kingdom Come: Deliverance is a rare example of an RPG based on medieval historical events that doesn't make you want to stick two fingers down your throat and lose your lunch. And while it takes plenty of liberties with history, the game still brilliantly captures the spirit of the era and manages to tell a far-from-boring story about a certain bastard.

Let me state right off the bat that I do not recommend playing the second part until you have finished the first. Franchise games are usually designed so that a player can jump in at any point and fully enjoy the experience, but that is not the case here. Even with the inclusion of flashbacks, there is still a wealth of information that requires having played the first game. That isn't a bad thing, though it is a relatively risky move for a big-budget project. Fortunately, the risk paid off.

Compared to the first game, the combat system has been slightly simplified. Henry can now wield early gunpowder pistols, crossbows, and polearms. While the gunpowder weapons and crossbows are fun to use, I can't say anything good about the polearms.

As for the main storyline, it is every bit as good as the first game's. There is still plenty of room for tense moments and drama, as well as a touch of comedy. The finale is particularly intense, though I do have reservations about the narrative's moral stance. Let’s just say I don’t quite subscribe to the philosophy that Henry should always turn the other cheek whenever possible. The game tries to teach that revenge is always wrong, yet the issue of impunity is never addressed. But that is the developer’s worldview — their message. There is nothing to be done about that.

You’ll find a handful of interesting stories among the side quests. Most of them didn't really stick in my memory, though. There are a great many tedious "fetch-and-carry" tasks that serve only as a means of earning money — honestly (or close enough to it). Speaking of the economy, getting rich in the game isn't particularly difficult, provided you don't mind looting fallen enemies and selling off the gear. Your main obstacle is simply the limited amount of Groschen in the merchants' purses.

As for the DLC content, I was largely disappointed. I can only praise *Mysteria Ecclesiae* for unlocking a new location and offering a reasonably interesting storyline. *Legacy of the Forge* failed to impress me due to its guild reputation system; I simply had no desire to grind just to complete a mini-storyline, especially since the opening setup made the ending all too predictable. As for *Brushes with Death*, it struck me as the most tedious and awful DLC of the lot. Instead of a mysterious artist, you get an annoying, schizophrenic whiner who constantly demands you complete the most boring tasks imaginable. His personal story is simply uninteresting. The remaining DLCs offer no narrative content — only gear that makes the early game significantly easier — so I chose not to use them.

I highly recommend the game, if only for its main storyline. It is superb — as are the antagonists and allies Henry encounters along the way. Clearly, the developers left room for the franchise to continue. We look forward to the third installment of the story.

I really do enjoy Black Desert online it has many facets I like.
What I do not like is what I will be focusing on this game, and although I would still recommend this game I would caution new players of some key facts.

Leveling: The leveling experience from lvl1-56 Is just a lot of running around and speed running dialog options and really has no meaning and if they deleted the low and mid leveling part of the game you wouldn't be missing anything at all honestly.

In game Market: Want to save silver to pay for premium because you don't or can't pay the overpriced fee? Tough luck you will not see them in the market and if you do you will never get one I know I've tried for over a year going as high as a billion silver. The reason for this is whales and spenders buy cosmetics as they sell for far more than the 30day premium service, this is based on the utterly insane and hyper inflated real money prices going for $20-$50+ real Dollars to buy which should not be the case but it is this is why you will be forced to stop playing for a month or so or be a new player to get the returning gift of a specific period of time of premium, they used to give out actual premium packs but when they changed the previously mention gift it seems they got rid of a lot of that. And it is a primary reason I do not play long term the second I run out of the free gift I stop playing because why should I be forced to pay? After all you are supposed to be able to buy with in game currency but you can't.

Life skills vs Progression: Season is a lot worse at this however it is kind of the same across the bored, the reality is for season characters they grind up to level61-63 Get all rewards rinse and repeat until all alts are the same level and at no point do you care about life skills. Life skills can be fun but unless you are only playing non-season there is no reason because it takes up grinding time.

Gear progression: Season gives you decent starter bossing gear it's not bad, however the base game gear progression system is about the most pathetic obnoxious system with so many layers and so many different required items not to mention if you try to grind out end game gear good luck it is based on a percentage success rate system which get's to a point where you are spending so much for so little but you need that little bonus to atk power or def power just to get anything done late game. Sometimes you get lucky and get free gear which is useable at lvl1 to use which can be nice to get as it negates months of grinding to at times over a years worth of grinding Absolutely NO GAME should force you to grind for that long period!.

Characters balance: Yeah let's just say there is a meta and if you are not using it end game feels underwhelming and even a newly released character is either overpowered or underpowered I hate meta focused systems because it means I cannot play the class I want and end up being forced to play what will be good for yet more grinding!

Granted I stated I recommend the game, why is that? Because compared to all other MMO's out there this game has far more going for it than any others which can be good or bad. You want to go onto open seas and go fishing? Okay go for it, want to be a farmer or breed horses? Go for it, want to be a hunter or lumberjack? Yeah they got that too, want to be a tradesmen, make potions, cook, or be a blacksmith? Let's go. And they are in-depth.

Lastly I would say there are things I'd love changed or updated but overall I know what I am getting into, and unlike many other games that force sluggish gameplay to reach end game on a seasonal character this game has them all beat as progression is very rapid, the storyline might be great.....But I have no idea I just hold R and skip all dialog because it is not engaging enough for me to care about.

For anyone who is new I would say give it a try it is worth the money as on sale you can get the game for like a dollar.

reviews.review:
Great gameplay loop that is very addicting, fun little story that is well contained with suitable challenges as you progress. A decent time sink and can be a nice second screen game once you've accomplished story objectives in whatever park you're in. The dinosaurs are cool and animated well, and there are a lot of feathered additions as well. You will still get the movie versions of most animals, but this game isn't really going for scientific accuracy.

I'm not a fan of the DLC pay structure for additional dinosaurs. I believe those should be released for free with major updates or as one large DLC that adds a new story campaign or significant challenges for players as opposed to multiple flavor packs. I have not played the Dominion expansion or any of the other additional content.

Getting 5 stars in each park was a good time if a bit repetitive. That said, the gameplay loop is what really drew me in. There is always one more thing to do, and that can lead to a lot of late night sessions where you promise yourself you'll go to bed as soon as the next thing is done. 

Would recommend on sale if you're not a big fan of the franchise. I certainly got my money's worth out of it.

Overall, if you are a fan of Owlcat's previous games, then this one would be somewhere between a 7.5 to 9 / 10 (really depends on how much you like 40k stuff). reviews.author: Gay Lord
reviews.review:
TL;DR: Game is good, but has A LOT of BS and *A LOT* of jank that requires getting accustomed to. That's where the actual difficulty comes from. The game itself is great! The world, graphics, music, bosses and combat are all so fun and satisfying. The multiplayer is AMAZING. The UI/GUI and the way the stats are all have that very mid 2000's/early 2010's semi-properly translated japanese RPG feel about them.

---------------------------------------

So, I got this game for free from Xbox Live Gold eons ago, back when that was a thing. I remember getting stuck at the tutorial demon (the plunge attack just DID NOT work!!) and then getting frustrated and swearing off any Souls games ever again. Years went by. Dark Souls 2, 3, bloodborne, Sekiro, Elden Ring all came out and despite the praise all those entries got, I still refused to play them. I was for sure that they games were NOT for me. 

That was until I got a 3DS and discovered Monster Hunter. Monster Hunter became one of my favorite series of all time. I knew Monster Hunter was similar in "difficulty" but figured it was still MUCH easier than the Souls games. Until I played World with a friend who got knocked around a lot by the monsters in that game. This same friend has thousands of hours and 100% achievements in every single FromSoft Souls game. I asked him why he's having so much trouble when he's literally a pro at the Souls games. He simply told me I should give the Souls games another chance if I find the difficulty in MH games fair.

Sooo, we played some co-op Elden Ring and I realized "I think I actually like these games?"

And that's how I'm back here, giving the game that started my initial hatred of the Souls games and Souls-like genre another chance. And I'm glad I did! 

Despite refusing to play these games, I did always love the dark fantasy universe these are all set in. The tone and setting of these games is wonderful. The bosses are often both grotesque AND cool, which fit the world pretty well. 

The combat is what kept me hooked, though. I loved Elden Ring almost instantly because of the way the combat feels, and it feels very similar in this game to. It has "weight" to it. Every strike feels powerful and every perfect dodge is so satisfying to perform.

The multiplayer is my second favorite thing about the game next to the combat. Seeing other players "phantoms", being able to be summoned or summon players to help on a tough boss. Seeing (often stupid) messages on the ground that others have left. Hearing the bells ring when an actual player rings them. It's incredible and makes the game feel so full of life. 

The level design and the encounters are the main difficulty of this game, not the fact you can get two-shot by something. It has A LOT of ambushes and sometimes throws half of an army at you out of nowhere. Or it'll put sniper archers with heat-seeking arrows ontop of a very narrow edge that you have to somehow get to them before they kill you. 

That BS mixed with the Jank of it being (I'm just assuming here) a somewhat low-budget JRPG game. Put them together and you have a "hard" game. The way the game works, the UI, the animations, everything feels like what early Monster Hunter felt like. Just very blocky and a lot of elements to get used to. 

It also doesn't help that everything in this game is cryptic and obscure. There's a ton of places you can go but never get even a hint that you can go there, so a lot of players miss out. (like Ash Lake). The way to start the DLC, you'd never find out on your own. (btw, do the dlc before the final boss. doing the final boss kicks you into NG+ instantly). You will DEFINITELY be looking stuff up on how to figure out how to do things.

The bosses, although all pretty well designed, some of them definitely felt purposefully unfair. The Ceaseless Discharge, for example. Everyone knows it's the "easiest" boss in the game due to a method you can do. I, however, wanted to try beating it the ""intended"" way. He has a MASSIVE cone-like fire attack that oneshots you, which he constantly spams when you die and try to get back up to him. The closet-like "arena" for the Caprademon mixed with having 2 dogs in there with him. The Gargoyle boss fight, having another one "come alive". Or even the Bed of Chaos which wasn't really a fight, but more of a dodging simulator to test your knowledge on how i-frames work. 

A big reason I never played these games before, and I'm not that interested in other Souls-Likes, is that I don't get that satisfaction of overcoming a tough boss after 50+ tries like a lot of people do. I don't go "YAY FINALLY I BEAT HIM I DID SO GOOD!". After beating a boss like that, my reaction is usually like "jesus christ that was annoying, i almost dropped the game because of that. atleast i can move on now"

Anyway, storytime and rambling over. Overall, the game is great and I highly recommend it. If you're having trouble, I HIGHLY encourage you to make use of summons. If you're still having trouble, I'd even recommend playing with a difficulty mod. Whatever makes the game fun for *YOU* is what is important.

If you are looking for a little respite from your usual hacking and slashing, this game offers a gentle take on action-adventure and introduces us to a magical world lead not by wand, but with music.

Forewarning: I am a baby of the Harry Potter era. So anything with witchcraft, automatically gets that reference. I am so (not) sorry >.< But I love how even tho my mind goes there, this isn't your usual HP remix. It introduces us to something new and I appreciate that so very much. The whole concept is built around music igniting magic in a soundless world. Everyone can harbour it with some direction and practice. It is within us all, all that differs is how we choose to express it. And so your journey to master your art begins....

Like HP, you are whisked off to school, you get mail, have a class schedule, can visit "Hogsmeade",  brew potions, practice herbology (gardening) and cast spells through the vessel of music. The game is heavily quest based, with concepts of collecting and crafting. This game doesn't limit you with timers. You have a calendar and events, but you cannot miss them. So get lost in the charm. The time stops during key sequences, allowing you to advance at a pace that works for you. 

Hands down, the best part of this game is the papercraft art that is both delicate and intricate, paired with perfectly whimsy music and voice over acting. You can completely customize your character to your liking, with lots of options available to change anytime throughout the game. The map is expansive, with so many nooks and crannies to admire. Oh yeah, and did I mention the cats? So an automatic win in my books ;)

I don't have any complaints. I did find the gardening introduction to spellcasting a bit weak and lacking. But I figured it out eventually with some trial and error. No sweat, just a little button smashing. 

Overall, this is a very relaxing play of discovery and exploring. It plays wonderfully on the steam deck. So sit back and have fun uncovering the magic that is inside us all.

reviews.author: Purplejump
reviews.review:
If you're a fan of highly interactive non-combat RPGs, this is the game for you! So far, I've only played about 4.9 hours, but already a lot of the quests, progression, visuals, and environment have been quite impressive. 

The art style is super unique, haven't really seen anything like it before, and it works so well with the tone of the game. The gameplay consists of you taking classes (which is how the game teaches you about mechanics, gives lore information, grants progression, and hands out more quests), tending to your garden (main way you make money and experience some fun building & optimization), exploring town, completing quests, and going to events! 

Like I said before, there isn't combat in the game which is a pretty nice change from all the RPGs that focus way too heavily on combat and make everything else feel pretty bland. This diversion from combat lets Songs of Glimmerwick make every quest feel pretty unique (at least so far).

Dialogue is fully voiced and generally pretty good at the time of this review, though occasionally things feel a bit weird. For example, one day almost everyone in the school is telling jokes, seems like that could've been spread out more, but maybe I'm just missing something and got unlucky.
